questions.question: Two containers of the same volume are 30% and 60% full of oil, respectively. They are then filled completely with water. If the contents of both containers are mixed in a larger vessel, what is the percentage of water in the final mixture?
questions.questionHtml: Two containers of the same volume are 30% and 60% full of oil, respectively. They are then filled completely with water. If the contents of both containers are mixed in a larger vessel, what is the percentage of water in the final mixture?
questions.solution:
⇒ Water in first container = 100% − 30% = 70%

⇒ Water in second container = 100% − 60% = 40%

⇒ Final water percentage = [(70 + 40) ÷ (100 + 100)] × 100 = (110 ÷ 200) × 100 = 55%

questions.question: A shop ordered 8 kg of Type P tea and some additional kg of Type Q tea. The price of Type P per kg was four times that of Type Q. When the order was delivered, the quantities of the two types had been interchanged. This increased the bill by 50%. Find the ratio of the number of kilograms of Type P tea to the number of kilograms of Type Q tea in the original order.
questions.questionHtml: A shop ordered 8 kg of Type P tea and some additional kg of Type Q tea. The price of Type P per kg was four times that of Type Q. When the order was delivered, the quantities of the two types had been interchanged. This increased the bill by 50%. Find the ratio of the number of kilograms of Type P tea to the number of kilograms of Type Q tea in the original order.
questions.solution:
Let price of Q per kg = p.

Original cost = 8 × (4p) + x × p = p(32 + x).

Swapped cost = 8 × p + x × (4p) = p(8 + 4x).

p(8 + 4x) = 1.5 × p(32 + x).

8 + 4x = 48 + 1.5x.

4x − 1.5x = 40 ⇒ x = 16.

Ratio (P : Q) = 8 : 16 = 1 : 2.

questions.question: A store sells an appliance for Z, making a 30% profit. During a sale, they increase the marked price of the same appliance to 1.5Z. They then offer a special discount of 20% on this increased marked price. What will be the new percentage profit made by the store?
questions.questionHtml: A store sells an appliance for Z, making a 30% profit. During a sale, they increase the marked price of the same appliance to 1.5Z. They then offer a special discount of 20% on this increased marked price. What will be the new percentage profit made by the store?
questions.solution:
Cost Price = Z ÷ (1 + 0.3) ⇒ Cost Price = Z ÷ 1.3

Discounted Price = 1.5Z × (1 − 0.2) ⇒ Discounted Price = 1.5Z × 0.8 ⇒ Discounted Price = 1.2Z

New Profit = 1.2Z − (Z ÷ 1.3) ⇒ New Profit = 1.2Z − 0.7692Z ⇒ New Profit = 0.4308Z

New Profit Percentage = (0.4308Z ÷ (Z ÷ 1.3)) × 100 ⇒ New Profit Percentage = (0.4308 × 1.3) × 100 ⇒ New Profit Percentage = 56%

questions.question: A vendor bought 300 mugs for 1,200. 50 mugs broke and became unsellable. At what price per mug should he sell the remaining mugs to earn a profit of 40% on his total cost?
questions.questionHtml: A vendor bought 300 mugs for 1,200. 50 mugs broke and became unsellable. At what price per mug should he sell the remaining mugs to earn a profit of 40% on his total cost?
questions.solution:
Profit = (40 ÷ 100) × 1,200 ⇒ Profit = 480

Total selling price = 1,200 + 480 ⇒ Total selling price = 1,680

Selling price per mug = 1,680 ÷ (300 − 50) ⇒ Selling price per mug = 6.72

questions.question: A solution consists of acid and water in the ratio 7:5. If 6 litres of acid is added, the new ratio becomes 3:2 What is the original quantity of water in the solution?
questions.questionHtml: A solution consists of acid and water in the ratio 7:5. If 6 litres of acid is added, the new ratio becomes 3:2 What is the original quantity of water in the solution?
questions.solution:
Let original quantity of acid = 7x and water = 5x.

New ratio: (7x + 6) ÷ 5x = 13 ÷ 10.

⇒ 10(7x + 6) = 13 × 5x.

⇒ 70x + 60 = 65x.

⇒ 5x = 60, so x = 12.

Original quantity of water = 5x = 5 × 12 = 60 litres.

questions.question: A tank has a mixture of solutions X, Y, and Z in the ratio 5 : 4 : 1. 30 litres of this mixture is drained out, and then 10 litres of solution X and 5 litres of solution Z are added to the tank. If the resultant quantity of solution X is 11 litres more than the resultant quantity of solution Y, find the initial quantity of the mixture in the tank (in litres)?
questions.questionHtml: A tank has a mixture of solutions X, Y, and Z in the ratio 5 : 4 : 1. 30 litres of this mixture is drained out, and then 10 litres of solution X and 5 litres of solution Z are added to the tank. If the resultant quantity of solution X is 11 litres more than the resultant quantity of solution Y, find the initial quantity of the mixture in the tank (in litres)?
questions.solution:
Let Q = initial quantity of the mixture.

Resultant X = Q × 0.5 − 15 + 10 = Q × 0.5 − 5

Resultant Y = Q × 0.4 − 12

Given: Q × 0.5 − 5 = (Q × 0.4 − 12) + 11

⇒ Q × 0.5 − Q × 0.4 = −1 + 5

⇒ Q × 0.1 = 4

⇒ Q = 4 ÷ 0.1 = 40

∴ Initial quantity of the mixture = 40 litres.

questions.question: A alone can complete a job in 10 days and B alone in 15 days. A and B agree to do the work for 6,000. With C's help, they finish it in 4 days. How much should C be paid?
questions.questionHtml: A alone can complete a job in 10 days and B alone in 15 days. A and B agree to do the work for 6,000. With C's help, they finish it in 4 days. How much should C be paid?
questions.solution:
⇒ Work done by A in 1 day = 1 ÷ 10 = 0.1, by B = 1 ÷ 15 = 0.0667.

⇒ Total work = LCM(10, 15) = 30 units; Work by A = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 units/day, by B = 30 ÷ 15 = 2 units/day.

⇒ Work by A, B, and C = 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5 units/day; Work by C = 7.5 − 5 = 2.5 units/day.

⇒ Total work by C = 2.5 × 4 = 10 units; Payment/unit = 6,000 ÷ 30 = 200.

⇒ Payment for C = 10 × 200 = 2,000.

questions.question: A circular garden has a radius of 10 m. A path of 4 m width runs around the garden. What is the area of the path? (Use pi = 3.14)
questions.questionHtml: A circular garden has a radius of 10 m. A path of 4 m width runs around the garden. What is the area of the path? (Use pi = 3.14)
questions.solution:
Radius of the larger circle ⇒ 10 + 4 = 14 m

Area of the larger circle ⇒ 3.14 × 142 = 3.14 × 196 = 615.44 m2

Area of the smaller circle ⇒ 3.14 × 102 = 3.14 × 100 = 314 m2

Area of the path ⇒ 615.44 − 314 = 301.44 m2

questions.question: Worker P takes 15 hours to complete a task, and Worker Q takes 20 hours. How many hours will they take to complete the task if they work together?
questions.questionHtml: Worker P takes 15 hours to complete a task, and Worker Q takes 20 hours. How many hours will they take to complete the task if they work together?
questions.solution:
LCM of 15 and 20 = 60 (Total work).

Worker P's work rate = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units/hour; Worker Q's work rate = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 units/hour.

Combined work rate = 4 + 3 = 7 units/hour; Time taken = 60 ÷ 7 ≈ 8.57 hours.

questions.question: Three friends, A, B, and C, are running on a circular track with a circumference of 5 km. They all start from the same point at 8:00 a.m. and travel in the same direction with speeds of 25 km/h, 40 km/h, and 50 km/h respectively. How many times will all three of them meet at the starting point if they continue running until 1:00 p.m.?
questions.questionHtml: Three friends, A, B, and C, are running on a circular track with a circumference of 5 km. They all start from the same point at 8:00 a.m. and travel in the same direction with speeds of 25 km/h, 40 km/h, and 50 km/h respectively. How many times will all three of them meet at the starting point if they continue running until 1:00 p.m.?
questions.solution:
⇒ Circumference = 5 km, Speeds: A = 25 km/h, B = 40 km/h, C = 50 km/h.

⇒ A lap time = 5 ÷ 25 = 0.2 h = 12 min; B lap time = 5 ÷ 40 = 0.125 h = 7.5 min; C lap time = 5 ÷ 50 = 0.1 h = 6 min.

⇒ LCM(12, 7.5, 6) = 60 min; Total duration = 13:00 − 8:00 = 5 h = 300 min.

⇒ Meetings occur every 60 min: 8:00, 9:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 13:00; Number of meetings = 300 ÷ 60 + 1 = 6.

questions.question: Convert 3.5 radians to degrees.
questions.questionHtml: Convert 3.5 radians to degrees.
questions.solution:
Let radians = 3.5

Degrees = radians × (180 ÷ π)

⇒ Degrees = 3.5 × (180 ÷ 3.1416) ≈ 200.54

questions.question: A sector of a circle having a radius of 12 cm has a central angle of π/4 radians. What is the area of the sector? (Use π = 3.14)
questions.questionHtml: A sector of a circle having a radius of 12 cm has a central angle of  π/4 radians. What is the area of the sector? (Use π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
Area of sector = (1/2) × r2 × θ

⇒ Area of sector = (1/2) × 122 × π/4

⇒ Area of sector = 18π ≈ 56.52 cm2

questions.solution:

questions.question: If sin B - cos B = 2 cos B, then what is the value of cot B?
questions.questionHtml: If sin B - cos B = 2 cos B, then what is the value of cot B?
questions.solution:
sin B − cos B = 2 cos B

⇒ sin B = 3 cos B

⇒ cot B = cos B ÷ sin B = cos B ÷ (3 cos B) = 1 ÷ 3

∴ cot B = 1/3
